messages:
tanya: Noticed a cluster-wide bump in nvme SMART 'Temperature' warnings and scrub retries in us-central1 around 03:05 UTC. GPUs stuck on attach for a few seconds, causing pod backpressure. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/drive-health/nvme-health?var-region=us-central1 :thermometer:

eric: seeing same. attach_wait alert on 12 hosts. tail I/O latency shows small random spikes vs usual baseline. pattern looks thermal-correlated by host rack.

rachel: suspected cron scrub overlap with nightly batch scaling. scrub daemon logs show repeated IO retries and 'requeue due to busy' lines. here's a sample from /var/log/janitor.log on ip-10-0-22-45:

```
2026-03-18T03:05:12Z janitor[478]: scrub start partition nvme0n1p1
2026-03-18T03:05:14Z janitor[478]: SMART temp warning: 81C -> throttling
2026-03-18T03:05:16Z janitor[478]: io retry after EIO, backoff 200ms
2026-03-18T03:05:20Z janitor[478]: scrub reschedule due to queue_wait=420ms
```

rachel: SMART shows temp attribute creeping above threshold on specific models (PCIE-FlashX-9000).

tanya: ops-bot, can you surface which AZ/rack tags correspond to the top hosts?

ops-bot: hosts affected: ip-10-0-22-45, ip-10-0-22-47, ip-10-0-51-12, ip-10-0-51-14, ip-10-0-60-3. All in us-central1-a, racks 7-9.

eric: quick mitigation: delayed janitor scrubs for affected racks, lowered scrub_concurrency from 6 -> 1 for those nodes, and disabled background fstrim for 10m. commands used:

```
kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-22-45.redwood us.scrub.pause=true --overwrite
ssh ip-10-0-22-45 sudo sed -i 's/scrub_concurrency: 6/scrub_concurrency: 1/' /etc/janitor/config.yaml && sudo systemctl restart janitor
```
eric: also temporarily set the scheduler preference to avoid aggressive packing on those nodes: `kubectl label node ... capacity.hot=false`

sam: added a transient routing rule in the allocator to prefer nodes with nvme.temp < 70C for new GPU attaches. will monitor for 30m.

rachel: recommend we add a thermal-aware janitor throttle so scrub intensity decays when SMART temp > 75C or queue_wait > 200ms. file a follow-up?

tanya: yes — please create a small RFC. immediate next steps: 1) run a per-model firmware check on FlashX units, 2) schedule a controlled scrub-canary during low-traffic window, 3) update Optimize docs recommending staggered scrub windows per-rack.

ops-bot: [note] attach_wait.us-central1-a suppressed by operator action. incident window 03:05-03:16 UTC.

eric: logging a retro ticket with cost implications: lower concurrency increases attach latency for cleanup but avoids GPU attach failures; need a knob in Console to let teams pick "cleanup aggressiveness" per cluster.

tanya: thanks everyone — let's run the firmware health check and plan the canary for Saturday 02:00 UTC. :calendar:
